_note: Automation (the automation tab, opened when the machine is fully fixed and a pet brings home a tiny capsule machine): your active pet does ONE job at a time for you. A job has to be taught first ('coins'), and some only turn up later ('needs': an unlock id from data/unlocks.json 'opens'; until then the job isn't there at all). Moving your pet to another job stops the one it was doing. JOBS: 'machine' = your pet cranks its own little capsule machine: one capsule a pull, worth the same as a plain capsule of yours (Machine.coin_value, so machine upgrades raise it), one pull every 'seconds' (made faster by tools). No lucky lights, no fever, no pet boxes: those stay with your lever. 'adventures' = your pet runs a party: it sends 'n' pets to a place, welcomes them back quietly when they're home and sends them out again (events pick their default). 'boxes' = your pet opens boxes from your pile (the cushion; it can't buy them until the piggy bank). TOOLS are what coins buy for a job: each level costs 'coins' x 'grow' to the power of the levels you have, 'max' 0 means no end; 'each' is what a level does: speed (the job goes this much faster, added up), away_hours (hours it keeps going while the game is closed; without it the machine stops when you close the game). 'color' is a UiTheme role, 'icon' a UiTheme doodle. WORKERS (the workers page, there once 'teach' is bought for a job: 'coins', and 'after' { tool id: level } of your pet's tools before it shows up): other pets do the job too, slower than your pet (half speed for a common, +0.1 a rarity step, see Automation.worker_speed). Each needs a 'spot' of its own, bought with coins ('coins' x 'grow' to the power of the spots you have): a machine, a box table, a party (an adventure party that keeps going, led by its worker, its pets drawn from the resting ones). You put the pets on yourself, and pets can't buy spots or boxes. Machine workers pull every 'seconds', box workers open a box every 'worker_seconds', both faster with 'worker_tools' (each: worker_speed). Workers keep going while the game is closed as long as your pet's stool lets it. 'army' = your pet leads the dungeon's army (data/dungeon.json): whenever the army is home it takes the same pets down again with the same orders (only while the game runs, and once when it loads); it's known as soon as floor 10 opens it (data/unlocks.json 'learns'), no teaching, no tools, no workers yet. Numbers are placeholders until balanced (priced at a few minutes of the lever when the tab opens, see docs/reports/pace.md). SPOT CAPS AND FLATTENING: machines and tables are old ones left in places you've taken; 'exist' { map page id: how many } is how many there are once that page is open (added up), 'per_place' how many per open place (parties). You can't buy past that (a save that already has more keeps them). Past 'flat_at' spots, each one costs 'grow_late' times the one before instead of 'grow', so thousands are possible. THE WHISTLE ('whistle', a find at the old well once you have enough workers, see data/adventures.json after_workers): managing is your pet's one job (task 'whistle', no teach price: the find is enough). Every 'check_seconds' (faster with the pencil: each check_speed) it checks on everyone: per job with workers two ticks, 'haul' (buy the next machine, table or party with coins, the cheapest first among ticked jobs, 'haul' a check plus the wagon's 'haul', never going under the coins set aside; 'keep' is where set aside starts, 'keep_steps' its - / + steps) and 'fill' (resting pets onto empty spots, the best first; parties first, leaving resting pets to go with them; empty parties get a leader, and a party is only hauled home while someone's free to lead it). It keeps checking while the game is closed as long as the stool lets it.
